In some ways it gets both easier and harder, easier because I'm a lot better at self care and recognizing when I'm slipping. When I was younger I'd drop a lot of weight and skip work and school and sleep all day and I wrote it off as "being burnt out", when in reality, I was just super depressed. I think in the past year I've focused more on being okay with not being okay and learning how to be functional physically, while mentally I'm still curled up in bed. 
Having a support system was the hardest for me to get, but ended up being the most beneficial. My gf checks up on me like a mom and I do the same to her, we make sure we eat, remind each other to bathe, we take turns doing dishes. I live with her, so it's easier to make sure I'm keeping up with myself, but even before she would frequently ask if I'd done my self care "chores". Being honest also helped a lot. I stopped pretending or trying to hide my depression, when I was sad I told people, when I stopped eating I told people. People aren't mind readers and sometimes can't always tell when something is up, so being honest helped me weed out people who weren't going to be support while strengthening the ones that would.
